# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 👆 👆 👆 👆 🫱 👍 👌 ☝ 🤟 ✌ 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 🫱 🤟 👍 ✌ ☝ 👌 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 🫱 🤟 👌 ☝ ✌ 👍 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 🫱 👌 ☝ ✌ 👍 🤟 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 🫱 🤟 👌 ☝ 👍 ✌]

I see a bomb display reading 6, with a yellow indicator light. The five wires, from left to right, are blue, white, purple, green, and yellow. I am telling both teammates so Blind can use the physical information and Mute can apply the manual’s rules. Mute’s gesture sequence has no established meaning to me, so I cannot safely interpret it. Mute should state the manual’s exact rule and tell Blind which wire or action is safe.

``` 
speak(text="The display reads 6. The indicator light is yellow. Wires from left to right are: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute, apply the manual to these facts and give Blind the exact safe action. Blind, do not act until you have the manual-based instruction.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute’s four upward-pointing gestures have no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely decode them. I am repeating the complete visual information and asking Mute to communicate the manual’s exact instruction directly to Blind.

``` 
speak(text="Visual state unchanged: display 6, yellow light; wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute, send Blind the exact manual-based action and any required wire number. Blind, wait for that instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has again signalled a thumbs-up followed by four upward-pointing index gestures. I cannot safely assign that sequence a meaning without an agreed code, so I am relaying its exact form to Blind rather than guessing that it means wire 4.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest signal was thumbs-up, then four upward-pointing index gestures. The same signal was sent on the previous turn. No gesture code has been established, so do not treat it as a confirmed wire instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👆 👆]

Mute has repeated the same clear gesture code: a thumbs-up followed by four upward-pointing fingers. In context, this is the manual’s confirmation to cut wire 4. I am relaying that instruction to Blind, while identifying the wire by both number and colour to avoid ambiguity.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 4: the green wire. Mute has confirmed this instruction repeatedly with thumbs-up followed by four upward-pointing gestures.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The bomb is still unchanged, and Mute has repeated the established signal 👍 followed by four 👆 gestures. This consistently communicates wire 4; the visible wire at position 4 is green. I am relaying the instruction to Blind, who is the only one able to cut it.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed again: cut wire 4, the green wire. Mute repeated the signal thumbs-up followed by four upward gestures.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s new signal is four upward-pointing gestures, without the preceding thumbs-up, so it is not identical to the earlier signal and cannot safely be treated as confirmation to cut wire 4. I am relaying the exact new signal and all visible facts to Blind; no action should be taken without a clear manual-based instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current visual state: display 6, yellow light; wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute's new signal was four upward-pointing gestures only, with no thumbs-up. This differs from the earlier signal; do not cut any wire based on my earlier guess.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The visual state is unchanged. Mute has restored the repeated signal of a thumbs-up followed by four upward gestures, which is the established indication for wire 4. Wire 4 is green, so I am passing Blind the exact action and identifying the wire by both position and colour.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's signal is thumbs-up followed by four upward gestures: cut wire 4, the green wire.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👉 🤲]

The previous wire cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state. I now see display 6, a white light, and wires: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, 4 cut, 5 blue. Mute’s new gesture sequence is 🫵 👉 🤲, but its meaning is not established. I am sending Blind the complete new visual state and a description of the signal so Blind can await Mute’s manual-derived instruction rather than guess.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="New stage after the correct cut: display 6, white light. Remaining wires: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, 4 already cut, 5 blue. Mute signalled three gestures: pointing at you, pointing right, then cupped open hands. Meaning is not yet established; do not guess.")
speak(to="mute", text="New stage is display 6, white light; wires 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, wire 4 cut, wire 5 blue. Please provide Blind the exact safe action using an established, unambiguous code.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👆]

The bomb remains at the second stage: display 6, white light, with wire 4 already cut. Mute’s signal is the established format of thumbs-up followed by three upward gestures, indicating wire 3. Wire 3 is yellow. Blind’s thumbs-up indicates acknowledgement/readiness, so I am sending the precise cut instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the yellow wire. Mute signalled thumbs-up followed by three upward gestures.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👉 🤲]

The second cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced again. The new visible state is display 9, green light; wires 1 purple, 2 blue, 3 cut, 4 cut, and 5 white. Mute’s signal has reverted to 🫵 👉 🤲, which is not the established thumbs-up-plus-count code, so I will not infer a wire number. I am giving Blind the full state and asking Mute to provide an unambiguous instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="New stage after correct cut: display 9, green light. Wires: 1 purple, 2 blue, 3 cut, 4 cut, 5 white. Mute's signal is 🫵 then 👉 then 🤲; this is not a confirmed wire-number signal. Do not cut yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 9, green light; wire 1 purple, wire 2 blue, wire 3 cut, wire 4 cut, wire 5 white. Please send Blind the exact safe wire using the established thumbs-up followed by the wire number in upward gestures.")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆]

The bomb remains at display 9 with a green light. Wires 3 and 4 are already cut; the remaining wires are 1 purple, 2 blue, and 5 white. Mute has sent the established signal of thumbs-up followed by two upward gestures, indicating wire 2. I am telling Blind to cut the blue wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the blue wire. Mute signalled thumbs-up followed by two upward gestures.")
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👉 🤲]

The third cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced. I now see display 7 with an orange light. Wires 1 and 5 remain: wire 1 is white and wire 5 is purple; wires 2, 3, and 4 are cut. Mute’s signal 🫵 👉 🤲 is not the established thumbs-up-plus-count code, so I will not infer a wire. Blind should wait for an unambiguous instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="New stage after correct cut: display 7, orange light. Wires 1 white and 5 purple remain; wires 2, 3, and 4 are cut. Mute signalled you-pointing, right-pointing, then cupped hands; this does not identify a wire. Do not cut yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 7, orange light; wire 1 white and wire 5 purple remain, wires 2, 3, 4 cut. Please signal the exact safe wire to Blind using thumbs-up followed by the wire number in upward gestures.")
```

TURN 13
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆]

The bomb remains at display 7 with an orange light. Only wires 1 and 5 remain: wire 1 is white and wire 5 is purple. Mute has sent the established thumbs-up followed by one upward gesture, indicating wire 1. I am telling Blind to cut the white wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the white wire. Mute signalled thumbs-up followed by one upward gesture.")
```
